To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RNMT T77 is phosphorylated by CDK1 cyclins B1, and this phosphorylation activates RNMT and promotes the production of a cohort of proteins required for cell proliferation.
CDK1 phosphorylates the T77 residue of RNMT, and that RNMT T77 is phosphorylated during G2/M to activate RNMT at the beginning of the G1 phase.
CDK1 activates RNMT by phosphorylation at T77 during the G2/M to G1 phase transition of the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of CDK1 cyclins in regulating RNMT activity.
the mechanisms of RNA cap methylation and the role of this modification in cell growth and proliferation.
the mechanisms by which the cap methyltransferase RNMT is activated and the consequences of RNMT activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNMT T77 is phosphorylated by CDK1 during G2/M and that the phosphorylation is required to activate the methyltransferase and promote the G1 phase of the cell division cycle.
CDK1 phosphorylates RNMT on residue T77 in a cell cycle dependent manner and that this modification is important for the production of proteins required for cell proliferation and cell division.
CDK1 phosphorylation of RNMT at T77 activates RNMT, coordinating mRNA cap methylation with G1 phase transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNMT T77 is phosphorylated by CDK1 cyclins B1, activating m7G cap methylation, which is required for efficient mRNA translation and protein production.

the CDK1 cyclins B1 and A activate RNMT during the G2/M transition, which coordinates m7G cap formation with the burst of nuclear transcription that occurs following mitotic exit and nuclear envelope reformation.
RNMT T77 is phosphorylated by cyclin B1 CDK1 in G2/M phase, resulting in RNMT activation, and that this activation is required for the G1 phase burst of transcription and for cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CDK1 cyclins B1 and A2 coordinate the production of translation competent mRNA with the onset of transcription.

the RNMT T77 site is an important regulator of RNMT function and that RNMT T77 regulation is a critical step in coordinating the production of translation competent mRNA with the burst of G1 phase transcription.
RNMT T77 is a CDK1 cyclinc B1 phosphorylation target that is required for the proper timing and amount of mRNA cap methylation during the cell cycle.
